evidence.title: Warfarin with aspirin or ibuprofen increases bleeding risk
evidence.section: Drug Interactions - Drugs that Increase Bleeding Risk
evidence.summary: The warfarin label lists aspirin among antiplatelet agents and ibuprofen among NSAIDs that increase bleeding risk when used with warfarin.

evidence.title: Lisinopril and hyperkalemia
evidence.summary: The lisinopril label states that renin-angiotensin system inhibitors can cause hyperkalemia and recommends periodic serum potassium monitoring.

evidence.title: Lisinopril with NSAIDs can worsen renal function
evidence.summary: The lisinopril label warns that concomitant NSAID use can deteriorate renal function in susceptible patients and advises periodic renal-function monitoring.

evidence.title: Metformin is contraindicated below eGFR 30
evidence.section: Dosage and Administration - Renal Impairment; Contraindications
evidence.summary: The metformin label states that use is contraindicated when eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2.

evidence.title: Insulin glargine and hypoglycemia
evidence.summary: The insulin glargine label identifies hypoglycemia as the most common adverse reaction and notes that severe hypoglycemia can be life-threatening.

evidence.title: ADA hypoglycemia thresholds
evidence.source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
evidence.summary: ADA defines level 1 hypoglycemia below 70 mg/dL and level 2 hypoglycemia below 54 mg/dL.

evidence.title: Warfarin INR above 4 is associated with higher bleeding risk
evidence.summary: The warfarin label states that INR above 4 generally provides no added therapeutic benefit for most patients and is associated with higher bleeding risk.
